channel.title: Kurs Media
channel.description: Russian business conflicts, money and power: what happened, what it costs and who benefits.

item.title: "A little bit different shape": what Russia, the US and Ukraine bring to Abu Dhabi
item.description: The first three-way talks between Russia, the US and Ukraine in nine months open in Abu Dhabi. Who is going, what changed during the pause, and why Europe was left outside.

item.title: Karapetyan's arrest and the nationalisation of Electric Networks of Armenia: what happens to Tashir's assets
item.description: The founder of Tashir has been arrested again, this time in a case over damage to Electric Networks of Armenia, which the state will nationalise in 2027. Who is who and what comes next.

item.title: The city and its shadow: why the Moscow region has never caught up with Moscow
item.description: Moscow spends three times more per resident than the region around it. How the Moscow region lived through the 1990s, debt and garbage protests, and why its towns still lag.

item.title: "Alexei Alexandrovich" and the "lambada dancers": why Severstal is taking a Russian governor to court
item.description: The Vologda governor accused people around steel tycoon Alexei Mordashov of a smear campaign. Severstal called it a lie and is preparing a lawsuit. How it came to this.

item.title: An SBU general, acid for a journalist and protection for call centres: what is known about the new stage of Ukraine's "Carthage" case
item.description: Ukraine's anti-corruption agencies reached the SBU leadership: a general detained, detectives threatened with a gun. Who is who in the case and what comes next.

item.title: Rostec director Vasily Brovko proposes Russia as an "ark" for the world. A review of his treatise
item.description: A Rostec director writes of the end of finance capital, "techno-fascism" and Russia as an ark. Which of his claims match the data and which do not.

item.title: Usmanov wins the right to sue the EU Council in Germany
item.description: Germany's top civil court ruled that refusing to serve Alisher Usmanov's reputation claim on the EU Council was unlawful. What it means for sanctions cases.

item.title: Russia and Poland: four centuries of friendship and enmity, from the Time of Troubles and Katyn to the Smolensk crash
item.description: How Russia and Poland fought and reconciled over four centuries: 1612, the partitions, Katyn, Solidarity, early Putin, the Smolensk crash and the rupture after 2022.

item.title: Poland: judges backed by Tusk's coalition oust the head of the Constitutional Tribunal
item.description: President Nawrocki called it a 'forcible takeover' and entered the court at night. Who is who, what happens on 3 November and what it means for markets.

item.title: A whole life for 99 rubles: who sells Russians' personal data, and why the market won't die
item.description: How Russia's Telegram lookup bots work, from Eye of God to Himera and NOX: the biggest leaks, arrests of their creators, a new criminal law and the risks.

item.title: "Soon is an elastic concept": the Kremlin responds to Trump on a Putin–Zelensky meeting
item.description: Trump promised a meeting with Putin and Zelensky soon. Kremlin spokesman Peskov said lengthy work must come first and that "soon" is an elastic concept.

item.title: Alexander Zharov: media technology must be our own
item.description: Gazprom-Media's Alexander Zharov calls media technology a sovereignty issue as RUTUBE hits 20m daily viewers and targets 7bn rubles in ads.

item.title: Russian gas in Alaska? The Polar LNG project faces claims of hidden ties to Novatek
item.description: A former Polar LNG chief says Novatek secretly funded the Alaska LNG plant. The companies deny it; the project seeks a US Treasury licence.

item.title: Copies by court order: Russia keeps a compulsory licence on Vertex's Trikafta, but bans Axelpharm's ruxolitinib generic
item.description: Russia's Supreme Court kept MIK's licence on Vertex patents for a Trikafta copy, while a court barred Axelpharm from selling ruxolitinib until 2028.

item.title: Banks v. telecom operators: Russia's fight over who pays for the networks
item.description: Russia's big four mobile operators and its largest banks are fighting over money: first fees for labelling bank calls, now curbs on bank-owned virtual operators.

item.title: Shelf price vs. register price: FTC and 20 states sue Dollar General over overcharges
item.description: The FTC and 20 states have sued Dollar General, alleging the 21,000-store discount chain charged shoppers more at the register than on its shelves for years.

item.title: Sanctions with interest: Rusal seeks $1.3 billion from Rio Tinto and takes aim at Mongolian copper
item.description: A Russian court has ordered Rio Tinto to pay Rusal $1.278 billion and levied execution on Rio's 66% stake in the operator of Mongolia's Oyu Tolgoi copper mine.

item.title: Rusnano v. Chubais: bailiffs pursue nearly 20 billion rubles over a failed school tablet and MRAM chips
item.description: Bailiffs have opened 14 enforcement proceedings worth nearly 20 billion rubles against ex-Rusnano chief Anatoly Chubais over the Plastic Logic and Crocus projects.
